Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "hey, can you help me write the request for a community survey export for the Brookmere Community Association? We ran a survey about possible uses and opening times for the ground-floor room in Beacon Hall, which is currently being considered as a neighborhood shared room. The survey was open from May 6 through May 24, 2025. People could answer online or return a paper form at the library desk. There are 186 submitted responses in the collected material, and two staff practice forms are marked TEST. I need an export of the survey responses, not a report about what residents think or a recommendation about the room. We have a planning meeting on June 3, so the file should be usable for reviewing the answers beforehand.

The main thing is a CSV with one row per submitted response. Keep the 186 resident submissions, including forms that have some unanswered questions; don't fill blanks by guessing. Leave the two staff practice forms out because they're marked TEST. Give each included response an anonymous response ID, and include the submission date and time in local time, the collection channel (online or paper), and the postal zone as entered on the form. The survey asked about age band and household type, preferred room uses, preferred weekday, and whether someone agreed to follow-up. Please include those answers too. For the preferred room uses, people could choose more than one option, so keep each person's selected options together in that field, separated by semicolons. We need to be able to tell which selections came from the same response, not split them into separate rows.

There was also an open comment box. Keep those comments in the residents' own words, including spelling and punctuation, rather than tidying or summarizing them. If the comment box was left empty, leave it blank. One resident wrote, “I could use the room after the library closes, especially in winter.” That's the sort of comment I mean; it should stay as a comment, not be converted into a category or a finding. The response export should not include respondents' names, email addresses, phone numbers, or any other contact details. There is a separate contact list for people who agreed to follow up, but that list is not part of this export; the consent answer can remain in the survey row as yes, no, or blank.

Could the request make the fields easy to identify? The form labels are not all obvious if you have not seen the survey. Use these column names in the CSV: response_id, submitted_at_local, collection_channel, postal_zone, age_band, household_type, preferred_room_uses, preferred_weekday, open_comment, and follow_up_consent. Keep the values as they were recorded, apart from the anonymous ID and the consistent online or paper labels for the channel. For unanswered fields use an empty cell, not a guessed value or a phrase like “not applicable.” For checkboxes in preferred_room_uses, use semicolons between selections. Please also include a small field key that explains each column in plain language, so someone at the meeting can understand it without needing the original form beside them.

The forms came in through two routes, and the paper forms were entered into the same collection workbook as the online replies. The paper route was the library desk, not a separate survey or a later round. We don't need a separate worksheet for each channel, and we don't need charts, totals by age, or a comparison of paper and online answers. Keep one response per row in the one CSV. The two marked TEST forms should not appear in the file or in any response count given alongside it. Don't change the meaning of a resident's answer to make the entries look consistent; for example, leave the postal zone as entered rather than correcting it from another source.

Please include a brief note with the export saying that the survey dates were May 6–24, 2025, and that online and paper responses are both included. The note can identify the survey as the Brookmere Community Association survey about possible uses and opening times for the Beacon Hall ground-floor room. It should not interpret the comments, give a response-rate estimate, or draw conclusions. The field key and note are just there to make the file usable for the June 3 planning meeting, not to turn it into a presentation.

Send the review copy to Saskia, not Bram. Bram has been helping with the room schedule, but he isn't the person who should receive this export. Saskia will check the columns and the handling of the paper forms before the meeting. The association will keep the original workbook and the separate follow-up contact list in their existing folders; this request is only for the response CSV, the field key, and the brief note. We have not decided the room's hours yet, and the export should leave that decision for the June 3 discussion.", "output": "Create a community survey export request for the Brookmere Community Association. The survey concerns possible uses and opening times for the ground-floor room in Beacon Hall, which is being considered as a neighborhood shared room. It ran from May 6 through May 24, 2025, and responses were collected online and on paper forms returned at the library desk. The collected material contains 186 submitted resident responses and two staff practice forms marked TEST.

Prepare a CSV with one row per resident submission. Include all 186 submissions, including partially completed forms, and exclude the two forms marked TEST. Do not fill unanswered questions by guessing. Assign each included response an anonymous ID. Use these column names:

1. response_id
2. submitted_at_local
3. collection_channel
4. postal_zone
5. age_band
6. household_type
7. preferred_room_uses
8. preferred_weekday
9. open_comment
10. follow_up_consent

Include the submission date and time in local time, the postal zone as entered on the form, and the answers to the questions about age band, household type, preferred room uses, preferred weekday, and follow-up consent. Use consistent values of “online” or “paper” for the collection channel. Respondents could select multiple preferred room uses; keep all of each person's selections together in that field, separated by semicolons, so it remains clear which selections belong to the same response. For unanswered fields, use an empty cell. Do not substitute a guessed value or “not applicable.”

Keep open comments in residents' own words, including their spelling and punctuation. Do not edit or summarize comments, and leave the field blank if no comment was provided. For example, one resident wrote, “I could use the room after the library closes, especially in winter.” Retain comments as comments rather than turning them into categories or findings. Do not include respondents' names, email addresses, phone numbers, or other contact details. The separate contact list for people who agreed to follow up is not part of this export. Keep the follow-up consent answer in the survey row as yes, no, or blank.

Add a small field key that explains each CSV column in plain language for people reviewing the file at the planning meeting. Also provide a brief note identifying the survey as the Brookmere Community Association survey about possible uses and opening times for Beacon Hall's ground-floor room. State that it ran May 6–24, 2025, and that it includes both online and paper responses. The note should not interpret comments, estimate a response rate, or draw conclusions.

The paper forms were entered into the same collection workbook as the online replies. They came through the library desk and were not a separate survey or a later round. Keep all responses in one CSV, with one response per row; do not make separate worksheets by channel. Do not add charts, totals by age, or a comparison of paper and online answers. Do not change the meaning of residents' answers to make entries look consistent. In particular, retain each postal zone as entered rather than correcting it from another source. Do not include the two TEST forms in the file or in any response count provided with it.

The export is for review before the association's June 3 planning meeting. Send the review copy to Saskia, not Bram. Bram has been helping with the room schedule, but Saskia is the intended recipient and will check the columns and handling of paper forms before the meeting. The association will keep the original workbook and separate follow-up contact list in their existing folders. This request is only for the response CSV, the field key, and the brief note. The room's hours have not been decided; leave that decision for the June 3 discussion."}]
